title: NGINX2Root (CVE-2026-123007): Frequently asked questions about five critical NGINX vulnerabilities
content_md: Frequently asked questions about five critical NGINX remote code execution vulnerabilities and five additional flaws fixed in F5’s November 18 out-of-band release. Key takeaways NGINX2Root is associated with five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and a separate, unpatched Linux kernel local privilege escalation (LPE) flaw that can be chained with the NGINX bugs to gain root. CVE-2026-123007 is the most urgent of the five. It is an unauthenticated RCE flaw in NGINX’s HTTP/2 implementation and requires only HTTP/2 over TLS to be enabled. A PoC is publicly available on GitHub. F5’s November 18 release fixed the five NGINX2Root vulnerabilities and five additional NGINX flaws. Background Tenable’s Research Special Operations (RSO) team has compiled this blog to answer Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) regarding NGINX2Root, a set of five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and five additional NGINX flaws that F5 fixed in an out-of-band security release on November 18, 2026. FAQ What is NGINX2Root? NGINX2Root is the name Xint (Theori) gave to five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and a separate, unpatched Linux kernel local privilege escalation (LPE) flaw that Xint says can be chained with the NGINX bugs to gain root. The NGINX flaws are memory-corruption bugs in HTTP/2, HTTP/3, the resolver, and the mail proxy module.
